title: Lior and the Typewriter
premise: In 1848, in a river town whose bridge closes each winter, Marguerite Almeida works her late father's type-cutting bench in a print shop that quietly prints pamphlets for both sides of a coming revolution. Years ago, in peacetime, she promised her friend Lior—a printer's apprentice now branded an enemy agitator—that if he ever needed hiding, the shop would keep him. When the bridge shuts early and soldiers seal the crossings, Lior arrives wounded at her door, and Marguerite must choose between loyalty to her neighbors and the truth of her promise. She hides him inside the type cases themselves, forging documents to move him out with the spring thaw, but the shop's owner suspects and the garrison closes in. In the end, Marguerite sacrifices the shop—burning it to destroy evidence—and ferries Lior across the ice on the last night before the thaw, inheriting not her father's trade but his quiet defiance.
about_author: Sebastian Ashgrove is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in provincial archives. Their fiction draws on the marginalia, ledgers, and unsent letters found tucked inside old type cabinets.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the last market day before winter, Marguerite cuts type by day and listens to rumors by night: the revolution has reached the far bank, and the bridge will close weeks early. A soldier posts the decree on the print shop door while she watches from the window. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—the moment invisibility stops being a choice.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to the summer she and Lior swore their pact beside the cooling type-metal. Now he appears at midnight, feverish and hunted, and she hides him beneath the floor of the composing room. The emotional beat is the collision of memory and danger: the past self who made promises versus the present self who must pay for them.

chapters.title: What the Type Cases Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating between Marguerite and Lior. As she forges travel papers using her father's punches, the shop's owner grows suspicious, and a garrison officer requisitions the press to print wanted notices—with Lior's face among them. The emotional beat is rising claustrophobia: the tools of truth turned into instruments of the hunt, and trust fraying under close quarters.

chapters.title: The Last Night of Ice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Discovered and cornered, she sets fire to the shop to erase the forged documents, then leads Lior across the frozen river as the thaw cracks the ice behind them. The bridge reopens to soldiers finding only ash. The emotional beat is costly resolution: she loses her inheritance but keeps her word, stepping onto the far bank as someone no longer invisible.
